channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tashkent to Block Bus Validators During Fare Evasion Checks
item.description: Tashkent authorities will now block bus validators when checking for fare evasion. Passengers found without a valid ticket or unregistered entry will be fined. This measure, effective September 1, aims to enforce fare payment upon boarding, as mandated by a government decree. The fine for traveling without a ticket currently stands at 44,000 Uzbek soums.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Danish Foreign Minister, Discusses Partnership Opportunities
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen to discuss expanding bilateral relations. They noted significant progress in cooperation, including a fivefold increase in trade turnover and joint projects in various sectors. Both sides emphasized strengthening trade, attracting Danish investment and technology in energy, transport, and agriculture.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Senate Chair emphasizes reforms' impact on citizens' lives
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate Chair Tanzila Narbaeva stressed that the real effect of reforms must be felt in every person's life. She highlighted the expansion of international cooperation, particularly with South Korea, opening new economic and technological opportunities. Parliament's role in implementing agreements was also emphasized.

item.title: Kazakhstan Coach Admits Tactical Error After Moldova Loss
item.description: Kazakhstan's head coach, John van 't Schip, took responsibility for the team's Nations League defeat to Moldova. He stated the team lost the match in the first half, failing to adhere to the planned structure and making errors during ball possession that hampered pressing. Van 't Schip acknowledged a tactical mistake in midfield play.

item.title: Internet Quality Issues Resolved in 22 of 24 Problem Areas in East Kazakhstan Region
item.description: As part of the "Accessible Internet" national project, comprehensive work is underway in the East Kazakhstan region to improve internet quality. The Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Aerospace Industry's Telecommunications Committee has addressed issues in 22 out of 24 areas with poor connectivity. Plans include fiber-optic network expansion and satellite solutions for remote villages.

item.title: Mining Company Fined Over 100 Million Tenge for Environmental Law Violations
item.description: A mining company, "Vostoktsvetmet" LLC, has been fined over 100 million tenge for exceeding environmental emission standards. The East Kazakhstan region's prosecutor's office reported that the company failed to address the consequences of subsoil use at the "Yubileyno-Snegirikhinskoye" field. An unscheduled inspection revealed prolonged inaction, leading to the fine and a directive to rectify environmental damage.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Federation for Digital and Artificial Intelligence Sports
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Federation for Digital and Artificial Intelligence Sports was introduced at the Digital Bridge international forum in Astana. The federation's first event was an AI table tennis tournament where participants performed exercises tracked by AI via smartphone cameras. The initiative aims to promote physical activity through digital sports.

item.title: Search for Missing South Korean Tourist Intensified in Almaty Mountains
item.description: Search efforts for a missing South Korean citizen have been intensified in the Almaty mountains, near the Talgar Pass. The operation now involves 10 units of equipment and eight canine units, up from previous numbers. Approximately 130 people, including emergency services, police, and volunteers, are participating, utilizing drones and aviation.

item.title: UN Expert: Laws Guaranteeing Equality Don't Prevent Daily Discrimination Against Women
item.description: A UN Women expert stated that while laws may guarantee gender equality, daily practices continue to discriminate against women. Olga Osaulenko highlighted that societal perceptions can limit women's access to education and leadership roles, and state bodies may treat domestic violence as a private matter, despite legal protections.

item.title: Search and Rescue Operations for South Korean Citizen Continue in Almaty
item.description: Search and rescue operations for a South Korean citizen are ongoing in the Medeu district of Almaty, near the Talgar Pass. The complex terrain, large search area, and significant elevation changes complicate the efforts. Approximately 130 personnel, 10 units of equipment, 8 canine units, 11 drones, and aviation are involved.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Reach Key Agreements to Enhance Economic Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Investment, Industry, and Trade concluded a working visit to Muscat, significantly advancing economic relations between Uzbekistan and Oman. Discussions focused on increasing trade, industrial cooperation, logistics, energy, and tourism. Both sides agreed on concrete steps to strengthen the legal framework for bilateral relations.

item.title: Kazakhstan MPs Discuss Medical Professionals' Status and National Security
item.description: Kazakhstan's parliamentarians debated the professional status of medical workers in relation to national security. The discussion, part of drafting a new bill, included input from presidential advisors, government officials, and healthcare professionals. Key focus areas were legal and social protections, enhancing the profession's prestige, and strengthening healthcare personnel. Constructive proposals will be incorporated into the bill.

item.title: Tashkent Hosts Vocational Education Fair Connecting Uzbek Youth with German Employers
item.description: Tashkent hosted the 'BerufsEXPO-2026' vocational education and employment fair, linking Germany and Uzbekistan. Over 2,500 young people participated, seeking in-demand professions for the international labor market. The event facilitated direct interaction with employers and educational institutions, emphasizing the importance of language skills alongside professional qualifications for overseas employment.

item.title: Bahodir Yunusov appointed Deputy Chairman of National TV and Radio Company for Compliance
item.description: Bahodir Yunusov has been appointed Deputy Chairman of the Uzbekistan National TV and Radio Company for compliance and internal anti-corruption control. Previously, Yunusov served as head of a department in the Presidential Administration. He had also temporarily served as First Deputy Chairman of the MTRK and headed the "Uzbekistan" TV channel.

item.title: Uzbek President receives Danish Foreign Minister, discusses cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the Danish Foreign Minister. The parties noted significant potential for developing cooperation between the two countries in the fields of education, culture, and tourism. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Ecological audit: Why it is necessary for environmental protection and resource management
item.description: Environmental protection, rational resource use, and ecological safety are key priorities. An ecological audit, established by law, provides an independent assessment of compliance with environmental standards and promotes the adoption of green technologies. It systematically examines emissions, waste management, and resource utilization.

item.title: Zelensky claims Putin ordered violation of war rules during September attacks on Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered his military to disregard the rules of war during intensified attacks on Ukraine in September. These attacks targeted schools, hospitals, and data centers.

item.title: Kazakh Deputy Prime Minister Orders Acceleration of Atyrau Infrastructure Projects
item.description: Kazakh Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev inspected infrastructure modernization in the Atyrau region. He instructed responsible authorities to promptly address issues and avoid delays in ongoing projects, including sewage treatment plants and heating network upgrades. The initiative aims to reduce heat loss and improve overall infrastructure by 2030.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves New Criminal Norms to Strengthen Penalties for Criminal Groups
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis approved a law enhancing penalties for organized crime and public order offenses. The legislation introduces a new article criminalizing the financing of criminal groups, with potential exemptions for those who cooperate with authorities. It also establishes separate liability for aiding criminal groups through abuse of power.

item.title: Confidence Building Through Media in a Polarized World Discussed at CICA Forum in Baku
item.description: A panel session on the role of media in strengthening social unity and intercultural dialogue was held at the CICA Media Forum in Baku. Pakistani Minister Wajiha Qamar highlighted media's importance in fostering understanding amid polarization. Uzbekistan's Kobuljon Akhmedov emphasized the need for more such meetings and recognition of media's role in conveying information and culture.

item.title: Kazakhstan Forum Proposes Startup Creation in Flagship Industries
item.description: At the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum in Astana, Kazakhtelecom Chairman Bagdat Musin proposed creating innovative startups in Kazakhstan's flagship industries. He suggested AI startups should focus on solving problems in sectors like mining and agriculture to boost productivity and attract international capital.

item.title: G7 Countries to Release Up to 100 Million Barrels of Oil from Reserves
item.description: G7 countries have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel from strategic reserves, announced French President Emmanuel Macron. These measures aim to help lower oil product prices, particularly for diesel fuel, and will be implemented over four months.

item.title: Kazakh Parliament to Use AI for Verifying Responses to депутат's Inquiries
item.description: The Parliament of Kazakhstan has approved new rules for handling депутат's inquiries, incorporating artificial intelligence to automate document preparation and verify the completeness of responses. The decision, made by the bureau chaired by Speaker Aybek Dädebay, aims to enhance the effectiveness of these inquiries. Digital analytical tools, including AI, will be employed in this process.

item.title: Elon Musk to Lead Pentagon's New 'Meridian' Project on Future Warfare Methods
item.description: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, along with Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich, will lead the Pentagon's new 'Meridian' project focused on future warfare methods. This marks Musk's first official role in a US presidential administration since his departure from the Department of Government Efficiency. The project aims to identify critical areas and capabilities for the US.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Agriculture Ministry proposes limiting potato imports until March 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture proposes temporarily limiting potato imports until March 1, 2027. The ministry cites sufficient domestic production to meet demand and aims to help local farmers sell their harvest. Projections indicate Kyrgyzstan will produce 1.249 million tons of potatoes in 2026, exceeding the estimated annual need of 799,700 tons.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry comments on citizens stranded in Russian war zone
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry has acknowledged reports about Kazakh citizens stranded in Russian war zones. A ministry spokesperson stated that protecting citizens' rights abroad is a priority and that the ministry has experience in repatriating citizens from conflict areas. They urged direct contact from citizens or relatives for accurate information.

item.title: France proposes EU release 100 million barrels of oil products from reserves
item.description: France has proposed that the European Union release 100 million barrels of oil products from strategic reserves. The proposal includes 50 million barrels of diesel and 50 million barrels of oil. Germany is reportedly hesitant to tap into reserves unless there is a clear threat to supply security. The coordination of this release at the EU level remains uncertain.

item.title: Kazakhstan Drafts Bill on Medical Professionals' Status and Guarantees
item.description: Kazakhstan is preparing a draft law on the professional status and guarantees of medical workers. Legal and social protection for medics were discussed at a roundtable in Astana, initiated by lawmaker Dana Medeuova. The event focused on the professional status of medical workers as a factor in national security. Participants included lawmakers, presidential advisors, and healthcare experts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry of Transport Discusses Benefits of Border Crossing Digitalization
item.description: The Ministry of Transport of Kyrgyzstan has detailed the advantages of digitalizing border crossing points (BCPs). The process of controlling the situation at BCPs and processing payments is being automated using digital technologies. Currently, the situation at border crossings is monitored online around the clock.

item.title: Former UN Official Recalls Tokayev's Negotiating Skills in Documentary
item.description: A documentary film highlights the diplomatic career of Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, focusing on his negotiation style. Former UN Deputy Secretary-General Sergey Ordzhonikidze described Tokayev as an opponent who deeply understood issues, contributing to his authority both domestically and internationally. The film features insights from other diplomats and officials.

item.title: Ukraine Drones Strike Russian Oil Facilities; Russia Attacks Kyiv
item.description: Ukrainian drones targeted oil facilities in Volgograd and Samara overnight. Russian forces launched three attacks on Kyiv, damaging a metro bridge and a residential building, killing one person. President Putin, speaking at the Valdai Club, reiterated threats of nuclear weapons against the West and denied Russia initiated the conflict.

item.title: Almaty Airport Presents Growth Prospects for Air Cargo Services
item.description: The president of Almaty International Airport, Goker Kose, presented growth prospects for air cargo services at the Central Asia Air Cargo Summit in Tashkent. Key topics included infrastructure development, digitalization, operational efficiency, international standards, customs regulation, multimodal transport, and international partnerships. The summit was a platform for experience exchange and strengthening business ties.

item.title: Eleven Individuals Convicted for Cattle Rustling in Abai Region
item.description: A court in the Beskaragay district of the Abai Region has sentenced eleven people to prison terms of up to six years for repeated cattle rustling. The investigation was conducted by the Beskaragay District Police Department. One incident involved police stopping three suspicious vehicles near the village of Oндіріс in February 2026.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Assess Afghanistan's Evolving Role Post-U.S. Withdrawal
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek highlighted Afghanistan's changing regional significance. Despite the U.S. departure, Afghanistan remains a key consideration for surrounding states and influences regional security, economy, and connectivity, particularly for Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Faces Corruption Report, Billionaire Timur Turlov Sued, and Asian Games Medals
item.description: GRECO has released a report evaluating Kazakhstan's anti-corruption efforts. Russian authorities have filed a lawsuit against Kazakh billionaire Timur Turlov in Moscow. Additionally, the Kazakhstan team secured three gold medals at the Asian Games.

item.title: US Tech Firm Firebird Invests $10 Billion in Kazakhstan Data Center Valley
item.description: American technology company Firebird has chosen Kazakhstan for its significant investment, citing strategic energy allocation and 1 GW of power capacity as key factors. The company is developing a 'Data Center Valley' in Ekibastuz with an estimated total investment of $10 billion.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Penalties for Sexual Crimes Against Children Under 14
item.description: A recent incident of sexual assault on a five-year-old girl in Uzbekistan highlighted systemic issues in child protection. Following public outcry and a delay, a bill to increase penalties for sexual crimes against children under 14 has passed parliament. Experts discuss whether harsher punishment is the solution and how to prevent such violence.

item.title: Panjshir World Council Documents 66 Human Rights Violations in One Year
item.description: The Panjshir World Council reported documenting 66 human rights violations in the province over the past year. These include killings, torture, and enforced disappearances. Around 340 residents faced humiliation, threats, or detention, some linked to their ethnicity or origin from Panjshir.

item.title: Bishkek Discusses Admission of Kyrgyz Children to Russian Schools
item.description: Bishkek hosted a meeting between the Deputy Minister of Education of Kyrgyzstan and the Deputy Head of Rossotrudnichestvo to discuss the admission of Kyrgyz children to Russian educational institutions. The discussion focused on improving testing mechanisms, teacher professional development, student career guidance, and developing inclusive education. The possibility of a forum for school leaders was also considered.

item.title: Human Rights Watch Urges Parties to Conflict to Prevent Civilian Harm Amid Airstrikes
item.description: Following civilian casualties in Pakistani airstrikes on Kunar and Helmand provinces, Human Rights Watch researcher Fereshta Abbasi called on conflict parties to respect international humanitarian law. UNAMA confirmed at least 10 civilian deaths, while the EU also expressed regret and urged restraint and dialogue.
